chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sa'id, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the bones of the elephant, whether it is permissible to sell and buy them, specifically those from which combs are made. He said, 'There is no harm with it. My father had a comb or combs from it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy and sell elephant bones in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the commercial permissibility of elephant bones for crafting combs, grounding the ruling in the established precedent of his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS). This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of relying on the practical usage of the Imams to clarify the status of specific commodities within the broader context of *al-Gharar* (uncertainty) and trade. The ruling underscores that items with clear utility and known origin are exempt from prohibitions related to ambiguity in sales.
